title: Vermillion Trim
description: Lets Cinnabar be used as a trim material
body:
In 26.2, the Sulfur Caves were added, which introduced two new blocksets. Sulfur, which can be compacted and be used to make geysers in enough concentrations. And Cinnabar, which... is mostly decorative.

**Vermillion Trims** expands upon Cinnabar by giving it one more use: A trimming material!
Irl, Cinnabar was used for a brilliant red yet toxic pigment known as Vermillion. This datapack does something like that, allowing Cinnabar blocks to be used as a trim material. This provides a special deep orange trim, between the shades of redstone and resin. It also has a special purple-ish tinge as it gets to the darker points of its gradient.

![Image of cinnabar being used to trim armor](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/YKpbpy9U/images/68a91d1522105ecfdb241aba30b27987b559ef98.png)
![Image of vermillion trim material description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/YKpbpy9U/images/fe69f235b714a76c2145d1a4859327a4c9d0eed1.png)
![image of player wearing full set of vermillion trimmed armor](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/YKpbpy9U/images/e7d42c677541249b124791849163dd1e757b862a.png)

# JANK WARNING!
I'm new to datapacking, and trying to make Cinnabar's item form be used as a trim addition was painful. Cinnabar gotten from the Creative Inventory lacks the trim data component and will be rejected by the smithing table. In order to make cinnabar as a trim material work, I had to change the Cinnabar block's loot table to drop a cinnabar block item with the trim material component. So make sure to mine cinnabar in survival mode to actually use it for trimming!
This datapack works best for a new world (drop it on creation), and may not work well if added in an existing world (To my knowlege, I don't think cinnabar blocks can be gotten as loot and is only through mining the blocks in world)

# Installation Instructions
Make sure to download **_BOTH_** the Data and Resource zips. Place `vermillion_trim_resources` into your resource packs folder, while `vermillion_trim_data` should be placed as a data pack (drag and drop is your best friend here)
